clue.text: Can society see round Romeo's pretentious display

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the cathedral city's name goes around the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the classic crossword see
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a company of people can see past Romeo's showy display.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England, so it is a 'see' (a bishop's seat).
explanation.definitionFit: Tinselry is gaudy, cheap glitter, hence any showy or pretentious display.

clue.text: Fresco base two minutes away from impressive principality

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes those letters

parts.note: mint is British slang for excellent or impressive
Monaco is a principality on the Riviera
M is the abbreviation for minute, so two minutes gives two Ms

explanation.surface: A fresco's base is taken two minutes away from an impressive principality, like a travel note.
explanation.walkthrough: One M goes from each word: MINT loses its first letter and MONACO its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonaco is the final thin layer of plaster on which a fresco is painted, its base.

clue.text: Small piece of material male journalist inappropriately inserted into narrative

parts.note: a patch is a piece of fabric
a cock is a male bird
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A small scrap of cloth and a male reporter are clumsily worked into a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatchcock something into a text is to insert it awkwardly or incongruously.

clue.text: "Bonkers" caught in Foreign Office love match

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy, bonkers

indicators.note: the cricket letter sits within the following pair of pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A crazy romance is struck up in the Foreign Office, a love match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love match' reads as a romance, but 'match' alone is the definition: something you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A locofoco was a nineteenth-century self-igniting friction match.

clue.text: Antipodean crayfish, reddish brown when seen from below, free at last in British Isles

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom up turns the colour word around

parts.note: bay is a reddish-brown colour, as of a horse

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the British Isles letters

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for Isles

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word free is taken

explanation.surface: An Australian crayfish, reddish brown from beneath, is finally released in the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Yabbies are small freshwater crayfish of Australia, hence Antipodean.

clue.text: Adolescent female shuns reading, for one, in favour of combat sports ring

indicators.note: the girl drops the letter for reading
the dropped letter is replaced by the sports abbreviation

parts.note: a girl is a young female
reading is one of the three Rs, so R
MMA stands for mixed martial arts

explanation.surface: A teenage girl gives up books for cage fighting in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading, for one' is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimmal is a ring made of two or three interlocking hoops, a jointed finger ring.

clue.text: Form of Malay whiskey consumed in prison endlessly

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed inside the prison word
the prison word loses its last letter

parts.note: jail is a prison
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Malay type of whiskey is drunk in a prison without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawi is the Arabic-based script used to write the Malay language, a written form of it.

clue.text: Eat, at intervals, mangey unknown scales of certain moths

indicators.note: to scale is to climb, so in a down clue the whole string reads upwards

parts.note: to dine is to eat

indicators.note: every other letter of mangey is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Mangy creatures munch now and then on the wing scales of certain moths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' looks like the moths' wing scales, but it is the climbing signal: DINE + AGY + Z read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Zygaenid describes the Zygaenidae family, the burnet and forester moths.

clue.text: Onset of acne by bad area — your back, near the armpit

indicators.note: the start of the word acne gives its first letter

parts.note: by as in multiplication is the times sign X
ill means bad

indicators.note: the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A first spot of acne in a bad patch on your back, close to the armpit.
explanation.definitionFit: Axillary is the anatomical adjective relating to the axilla, the armpit.

clue.text: Walk that's covered in circulated Ordnance Survey article Wainwright's Ultimate Breaks

indicators.note: that final letter breaks into the reversed letters and article
the map-maker's letters are turned around

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for Ordnance Survey, Britain's mapping agency

indicators.note: the final letter of Wainwright's is used

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A covered walk is in a map firm's article on Wainwright's best walking breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Wainwright wrote famous fell-walking guides to the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greece, a sheltered walkway.

clue.text: Instrument once found in westbound stop flanking back of Seaham Harbour

indicators.note: the reversed word sits either side of the next letter
in an across clue going west is reading right to left

parts.note: to abort is to stop

indicators.note: the last letter of Seaham is taken

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for boats

explanation.surface: An old instrument turned up at a westbound stop by Seaham Harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaham is a seaside town in County Durham, England, with a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The tromba marina was a tall, single-stringed bowed instrument of medieval and Baroque times, now obsolete.

clue.text: Concerning brief sign in past error-recognition

parts.note: re means concerning

indicators.note: the shortened zodiac sign sits inside the word for past

parts.note: since can mean ago, in the past

indicators.note: the zodiac word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Pisces is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A short sign of a past mistake being recognised, about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Resipiscence is a recognition of one's errors, a return to a sounder mind.

clue.text: Mum and dad swapped books about language

indicators.note: the two family words appear in the other order

parts.note: pa is dad
mum as in keep mum means quiet, SH

indicators.note: the books abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad trade books about a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but here it means silent, giving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is the Iranian tongue of the Pashtuns, spoken in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: Emergence of outcry surrounding prime parts of policy being withdrawn

indicators.note: drawn back, so the whole thing reads backwards
the outcry word goes around the selected letters

parts.note: noise as in making a noise, an outcry
the letters of policy at the prime-numbered positions two, three and five

explanation.surface: An outcry rises as the main parts of a policy are pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' is not 'first' here: it means the prime-numbered positions, second, third and fifth, of policy; 'being withdrawn' then turns the whole assembly back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclosion is an insect's emergence from its pupa or egg.

clue.text: Homelessness days into house price surge

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the surge word

parts.note: a boom is a surge in prices
D is the abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: Days of homelessness follow a surge in house prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobodom is the state or world of hobos, tramps without a home.

clue.text: What upset docked horse scoffing north Mexican agave

indicators.note: eating, so the pieces take in the next letter
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what

indicators.note: the horse word has its tail cut off

parts.note: equine as a noun means a horse

explanation.surface: Puzzlement as a tail-trimmed horse munches northern Mexican agave.
explanation.definitionFit: Henequen (or henequin) is a Mexican agave grown for its sisal-like fibre.

clue.text: Blast fragment in bondstone

parts.note: a parp is a blast on a car horn
an end is a remnant or fragment

explanation.surface: A blast leaves a fragment lodged in the bondstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A parpend, or perpend, is a stone running through a wall's full thickness to tie it.

clue.text: Rigid, warm and dry drunk

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone stiff, warm and dry-throated but drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigid' is in the sense of an argument with no flaws to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight case is watertight, unassailable and firmly sealed, so rigid.

clue.text: Very smelly odours in mills

indicators.note: to mill is to grind and churn, so the letters are ground into a new order

explanation.surface: Mills full of rank smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it is part of the material that 'mills' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Nidorous means having the smell of burning or cooking meat, strong-smelling.

clue.text: Wickedness of lady exposed for hiding wrongdoing

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the wrong word
stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: madam is a polite form for a lady
harm is injury or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A lady's wickedness is exposed for covering up wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adharma is a Hindu and Buddhist concept of unrighteousness, wickedness opposed to dharma.

clue.text: Jimmy's laughed quietly, clad in female undies with no opening

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: wearing knickers is knickered

explanation.surface: Jimmy giggled, dressed in women's underwear that has lost its fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy is a stock name for a Scot, so 'Jimmy's' marks a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: To nicker is Scots for to snigger or laugh in a suppressed way.

clue.text: Stop Republican genius ignoring terms of US Secret Service

indicators.note: the selected letters are left out of the genius

parts.note: Einstein is the byword for a genius

indicators.note: terms are ends, so the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Secret Service agents halt a Republican mastermind.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of US, Secret and Service are S, T, E, which come out of EINSTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or halt, as you would a horse with the reins.

clue.text: Pale green shipping waterway in which diamonds delayed

indicators.note: the card letter is moved later in the waterway

parts.note: the Red Sea is a busy shipping route
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A pale green shipping lane where diamonds were held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda is a greyish-green colour, named after the mignonette plant.

clue.text: Regarding petty observation, David quite upset about it

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the last word
upset as in knocked over, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: David is rather upset by a petty remark about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidditative relates to quiddities, quibbles or trifling distinctions.

clue.text: Motor race nervous wife avoids

indicators.note: the wife letter steers clear, being removed

parts.note: windy is slang for nervous

explanation.surface: A nervous wife steers clear of a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy is short for the Indianapolis 500 or IndyCar motor racing.

clue.text: In the end, Amundsen first to pole having taken over old tip from Scott

indicators.note: the two letters take in the others
the last letter of Amundsen
the opening letter of pole

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Amundsen finally reached the Pole first, beating Scott in a polar race.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott here is Sir Walter Scott, whose Scots usage this is, not the explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noop is a Scots word, used by Walter Scott, for a knob or tip, as of the elbow.

clue.text: Symptom originating in Asian republic — India, I think …

parts.note: Indic means of or from India
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
um is a hesitant noise made while thinking

explanation.surface: A symptom first seen in an Asian country, India, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicium is an indicating mark or sign, as a symptom is of disease.

clue.text: Affected aircraftman with long hair

parts.note: AC is the RAF abbreviation for aircraftman
tressy means having tresses, long locks

explanation.surface: A vain airman sporting long hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Actressy means theatrical and showy, behaving in an affected, stagey way.
